Agents of the same type are stored contiguously. The input `percent_agents_per_type` (e.g., `[0.33+\\u03b2, 0.33\\u2212\\u03b2, 0.34]`) determines the fraction of each type. This function is not called inside any numba JIT loop \\u2014 it runs once before the simulation begins to fix the population composition.\\n\\n### Strategy profile representation: `profiles_indexed`, `repmultipliers`, `dimactions`\\n\\n**Paper connection (\\u00a73.1, \\u00a74.1):** \\\"Agents' strategy profiles can be expressed as strings of length 1 + \\u03b8 \\u2026 The first element in this string represents the social signal that an agent broadcasts and the subsequent elements represent the action that is played when paired with an agent who broadcasts the corresponding signal.\\\"\\n\\nThe paper's string representation is implemented as follows. Each strategy profile is a vector of length `sigdimensions + numsignals` (here 2 + 4 = 6 for the two-dimension, two-signal-per-dimension case in the single-embedding sweep). The first `sigdimensions` entries hold the signal broadcast in each dimension (0 = null/no signal, 1 or 2 = an active signal). The next `numsignals` entries hold the action taken when observing each of the possible combined signal indices (0\\u20133 in the 2\\u00d72 case). This directly implements the paper's description: \\\"the first element \\u2026 the social signal \\u2026 the subsequent elements \\u2026 the action that is played when paired with an agent who broadcasts the corresponding signal.\\\"\\n\\n`dimactions` lists the number of possible values at each position in the string: `[signals_in_dim_1, signals_in_dim_2, actions, actions, actions, actions]`. `repmultipliers` is the mixed-radix positional weight for each position, computed as a shifted cumulative product of `dimactions`. This maps each integer profile index uniquely to a profile string and back, enabling efficient storage of strategy profiles as single integers rather than full vectors.\\n\\n`profiles_indexed` is a lookup table of shape `(numprofiles, sigdimensions + numsignals)`, constructed inside the initialize functions, enumerating all possible strategy profiles in order. Entry `profiles_indexed[k]` gives the full string for profile k.\\n\\n### `replicator_initialize` and `replicatorexec_initialize`\\n\\n**Paper connection (\\u00a72.2):** \\\"We always begin simulations with agents whose strategy profiles are randomly assigned.\\\"\\n\\n**`replicator_initialize`** (used for the non-exec replicator) and **`replicatorexec_initialize`** (used for the exec replicator and also within the RL code to set up `profiles_indexed` and `sigperdim`) both: (a) set each agent's signal urn to a one-hot vector drawn uniformly at random from all signal options per dimension, (b) set each agent's receiver urn to a one-hot vector drawn uniformly at random from all actions, and (c) enumerate all possible strategy profiles into `profiles_indexed`. The one-hot representation of random initialization maps to the paper's \\\"randomly assigned strategy profiles\\\" \\u2014 each agent starts with a single definite strategy rather than a distribution over strategies.\\n\\n**`replicatorexec_initialize`** additionally allocates an `execurns` array (shape `[population_size, sigdimensions]`) that records whether each agent attends to each signaling dimension. This is inferred from the signal urn (null signal = not attending) and is used mainly for result reporting, not during the simulation dynamics themselves.\\n\\n### Signal and action urn representation\\n\\n**Paper connection (\\u00a73.3, Appendix B):** \\\"Each urn begins a simulation with one ball corresponding to each possible action for that location in the strategy profile string.\\\"\\n\\nThroughout both codebases, agent state is stored in two main arrays:\\n\\n- **`sigurns`**: a Python list of `sigdimensions` numpy arrays, each of shape `[population_size, signals_per_dim]`. Entry `sigurns[d][i][s]` is the weight (ball count) for agent `i` broadcasting signal `s` in dimension `d`. In the replicator, these are always one-hot. In the RL model, they begin at 1 for all entries and evolve continuously.\\n\\n- **`recurns`**: a numpy array of shape `[population_size, numsignals, numactions]`. Entry `recurns[i][signal_combo][action]` is the weight for agent `i` playing `action` upon observing combined signal index `signal_combo`. Again one-hot in the replicator, continuous in RL.\\n\\n### Signal cost\\n\\n**Paper connection (\\u00a73.3):** \\\"a signal cost, c, that an agent incurs if she broadcasts any signal other than 0. When an agent uses a nonzero signal, its payoff from an interaction is decreased by c.\\\"\\n\\nIn the notebook, `signal_cost` is set to a negative number (e.g., \\u22120.0005). In `executilcompute` and `executilcomputeREforget`, the cost is applied by computing `totalAsigcost = (number of non-null signal dimensions) \\u00d7 sigcostf`. This is then *added* to the raw payoff \\u2014 and because `sigcostf` is negative, the net effect is a deduction. Crucially, signal cost is applied on every interaction regardless of whether it results in successful coordination, matching the paper's statement that payoff is decreased for any agent using a nonzero signal.\\n\\nOne detail not stated explicitly in the paper: the cost is proportional to the number of active signaling dimensions, not simply a flat cost for \\\"using signals at all.\\\" This means agents attending to both signaling dimensions pay cost 2c per interaction. This is consistent with the paper's statement (\\u00a74.1) that \\\"we assume the signal cost c is incurred for each dimension attended to.\\\"\\n\\n### Null-signal interaction rule\\n\\n**Paper connection (\\u00a73.3):** \\\"When an agent does not attend to signals (i.e., when she broadcasts 0), she interacts with all other agents as if they had also broadcast 0.\\\"\\n\\nIn `executilcompute` and `executilcomputeREforget`, before computing which action A takes in response to B's signal, the code zeros out any dimension where *either* agent has a null signal (0) in that dimension:\\n```python\\nfor idx1212 in range(0, sigdimensionsf):\\n    if Aprofile_copy[idx1212] == 0 or Bprofile[idx1212] == 0:\\n        Aprofile_copy[idx1212] = 0\\n        Bprofile[idx1212] = 0\\n```\\nThe effective \\\"signal seen by A\\\" is then computed from B's zeroed-out profile. If B broadcasts null in all dimensions, the signal index seen by A is 0 in all dimensions, so A looks up `recurns[A][0]` \\u2014 their action for signal combination 0, which is exactly \\\"treating them as if they broadcast 0.\\\" The symmetry (zeroing both A and B if either is null) ensures mutual blindness.\\n\\n### Assortment / homophily\\n\\n**Paper connection (Appendix A, Appendix B):** H(h,x,i) = N / \\u03a3_j [S(h,x,j)] \\u00d7 S(h,x,i), where S(h,x,j) = 2^h for 1D signals (same signal), and for multiple dimensions S(h,x,j) = (2\\u00d7d)^h if the same signal in d dimensions, 1 otherwise.\\n\\nThe assortment computation is split across three functions:\\n\\n**`assort_array_create` / `execassort_array_create`**: Builds a static `[numsignals \\u00d7 numsignals]` lookup table of raw assortment weights. For signal pair (i, j), counts the number of signal dimensions where their values agree, then computes `base_connection_weights[d]^homophily_factor`. The `base_connection_weights` array is `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]`, so entry `d` gives 2^d. Together with the homophily exponent, this gives `(2^d)^h = 2^(d\\u00d7h)`. For d=1 and h=1, this yields 2, matching S(h,x,j) = 2^1 = 2 for one matching dimension. For d=0, `2^0 = 1` matching the baseline.\\n\\nThe exec variant (`execassort_array_create`) differs in one respect: it only counts dimensions where *both* signals are nonzero when tallying shared dimensions. This captures the intuition that two agents both broadcasting null in a dimension do not share a meaningful signal there.\\n\\n**`get_sig_counts` / `get_sig_countsRE`**: Counts how many agents in the current population are broadcasting each combined signal index. This provides the \\u03a3_j[S(h,x,j)] denominator needed for the normalization. The replicator version works from the profile count arrays; the RL version works from `agentprofilepicks` (the per-agent profile draws for the current timestep).\\n\\n**`find_assort_multipliers`**: For each signal pair (i, j), computes the final assort multiplier as `assort_array[i][j] \\u00d7 (N / \\u03a3_k assort_array[i][k] \\u00d7 count_k)`. This exactly implements N / \\u03a3_j[S(h,x,j)] \\u00d7 S(h,x,i) from the paper. The resulting matrix `assort_multipliers[i][j]` is then multiplied into every utility/payoff computation involving agents with signal i interacting with agents with signal j.\\n\\n### Convergence / early termination\\n\\n**Paper connection (Table 4, footnote 2 of Appendix E):** \\\"every 100 timesteps it was checked whether the distribution of agents' strategy profiles was unchanged. If so, the simulation was halted prior to reaching 4 \\u00d7 10^4 timesteps.\\\"\\n\\nBoth full-play functions include this check, but with different periodicity. The replicator checks every 100 timesteps (`if idxN0%100 == 0`) by comparing `agentprofilesCOPY` to `agentprofiles`. The RL model checks every 1,000 timesteps, comparing `agentprofilepicksCOPY` to `agentprofilepicks`. The RL model uses a longer interval because its stochastic per-timestep profile sampling means that even a stable urn configuration will produce different `agentprofilepicks` from timestep to timestep, making exact equality less diagnostic.\\n\\n### Output and results reporting\\n\\n**`genBSexec_results` / `genBS_resultsRE`**: Called at the end of each simulation run (and periodically as snapshots). Computes:\\n- `socialsig_aggregate[type][signal]`: count of agents of each type using each combined signal index as their modal signal.\\n- `action_aggregate[type][signal][action]`: distribution of actions taken by agents of each type in response to each signal.\\n- `simple_stat_001[y_type][x_type][action]`: records the most likely action that agents of type y take when encountering the most common signal of type x (using argmax throughout).\\n- `simple_stat_002[y_type][x_type][action]`: a stricter version requiring that >75% of type x uses that signal AND >75% of type y's responses to that signal are that action. This is the threshold used to classify a simulation outcome as having a \\\"clean\\\" behavioral pattern.\\n\\nThe paper's classification of outcomes (iv), (v), etc. in Appendix A, and outcomes (i)\\u2013(xiii) in Appendix G, are computed in the notebooks by inspecting `simple_stat_002` arrays across runs.\\n\\n**`time_update`**: Records time-series snapshots of the population's signaling and action distributions. This is used only for visualizing the evolution of individual simulation runs (Cells 12\\u201313 in the replicator notebook). It is not used for any cross-run aggregate statistics reported in the paper.\\n\\n**`getalphasignaling` / `getalphastyped0`**: Post-processing function called after all runs complete. Because the labeling of which signal is \\\"signal 1\\\" vs. \\\"signal 2\\\" is arbitrary across runs (the model has no fixed assignment of signals to groups), this function re-labels signals across runs so that type 0's (Lagashites') most common signal in a given dimension is consistently called \\\"alpha.\\\" This enables meaningful aggregation of signal distributions across many runs. The function also records `execsruns`, indicating for each type which signaling dimensions they most commonly attend to (inferred from whether their modal signal in that dimension is null or not). This is not mentioned explicitly in the paper but is an analysis tool for understanding which dimensions each type uses.\\n\\n**`mutual_info` / `average_mutual_info`**: Computes the Shannon mutual information between the signal broadcast by an agent and the action taken in response, averaged across the population. This is used to compute the synergistic information measure discussed in \\u00a74.3 of the paper in the context of intersectional identities. The paper cites Varley and Kaminski (2022) and partial information decomposition.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Part 3: Replicator Dynamics \\u2014 `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play` and Supporting Functions\\n\\nThis section covers all functions used in the replicator dynamics notebook and its `.py` file that are specific to the replicator path (i.e., not already covered in Part 2).\\n\\n### Main loop: `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play`\\n\\n**Paper connection (\\u00a72.2):** \\\"The model dynamics proceeded in discrete timesteps, using replicator dynamics under the assumption of a large number of interactions in a well-mixed population.\\\"\\n\\nThis function orchestrates the entire replicator simulation. The main loop runs from timestep 1 to `runlength` (nominally 4\\u00d710^4) with an early-termination check every 100 steps. The calling convention `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play_typed` is a thin wrapper that converts Python lists to numba-typed lists and back, required for numba's JIT compilation.\\n\\n### Initialization for replicator: `genBSreplicatorexec_k_step`\\n\\n**Paper connection (\\u00a72.2):** \\\"We always begin simulations with agents whose strategy profiles are randomly assigned.\\\"\\n\\nAfter the urn-based initialization (which sets up `profiles_indexed`), `genBSreplicatorexec_k_step` assigns each agent a profile index uniformly at random from all `numprofiles` possible profiles. This is conceptually equivalent to the paper's random initialization \\u2014 every possible strategy is equally likely to be assigned. The result is stored in `profile_count_typed[type][profile]` and `profile_count_untyped[profile]` (counts of agents of each type with each profile) plus `agentprofiles[agent]` (the profile index for each individual agent).\\n\\n### Utility computation: `executilcompute`\\n\\n**Paper connection (\\u00a72.2):** \\\"The utility of strategy profile x for preference type k is calculated as: Uk(x) = \\u03a3_{i\\u2208Y} [M(i) \\u00d7 p_{xi,k}] if x \\u2260 i, \\u03a3_{i\\u2208Y} [(M(i)-1) \\u00d7 p_{xi,k}] if x = i \\u2026 where M(i) is the number of agents (of any preference type) in the population who play strategy i, and p_{xi,k} is the payoff to an agent of preference type k for playing strategy x when paired with an agent who plays strategy i.\\\"\\n\\n**Appendix A:** \\\"U(x) = \\u03a3_{i\\u2208Y} [H(h,x,i) \\u00d7 M(i) \\u00d7 p_{xi}] if x \\u2260 i, \\u03a3_{i\\u2208Y} [H(h,x,i) \\u00d7 (M(i)-1) \\u00d7 p_{xi}] if x = i\\\"\\n\\n`executilcompute` implements the assortment-weighted utility function. For every pair of distinct profile types (A, B):\\n1. Computes the assortment multiplier H(h,A,B) = `assort_multipliers[assortsigA][assortsigB]` using the signal indices before null-zeroing (assortment depends on what signals agents actually broadcast, not on the effective signal seen after null-matching).\\n2. Applies null-signal zeroing to determine effective signal exchange.\\n3. Looks up A's action (from B's effective signal) and B's action (from A's effective signal).\\n4. Adds `hfmultiplier \\u00d7 M(B) \\u00d7 (coordination_preference[type][action] + signal_cost)` to the utility of profile A for each type (using M(B)-1 when A = B to exclude self-pairing). The signal cost is negative, effectively reducing payoffs.\\n5. When actions differ (coordination failure), `genBSpunishf` replaces the coordination preference. In the single-embedding sweep, `genBSpunish = 0`, so failures yield zero payoff.\\n\\nThe result is `profile_utility_bytype[type][profile]`, the total utility that an agent with profile A would accumulate across all its interactions with the current population, computed separately for each preference type.\\n\\n### Replicator update: `genBSreplicator_single_tstep`\\n\\n**Paper connection (\\u00a72.2):** \\\"N_{k,t+1}(x) = N_{k,t}(x) + N_{k,t}(x) \\u00d7 [Uk(x) - Avg(Uk(i))_{i\\u2208X}]\\\"\\n\\nThis function applies the discrete replicator equation. For each preference type k:\\n1. Zeros out utilities for profiles not currently present in type k's population (utilities are only meaningful for present profiles).\\n2. Computes the average utility across all present profiles of type k.\\n3. Updates each profile count: `profile_count_typed[k][x] += profile_count_typed[k][x] \\u00d7 (utility[k][x] - type_average[k])`.\\n4. Clamps any negative counts to zero (an artifact of discrete rounding when a profile's utility is far below average).\\n5. Renormalizes so the total count of each type remains constant at `typestotal[k]`.\\n6. Converts floating-point counts back to integer agent assignments through cumulative rounding, building `agentprofiles` as an ordered array where agents of each profile type are listed contiguously.\\n\\nThe renormalization (step 5) and the integer rounding (step 6) are implementation details not stated in the paper's equation but necessary for a discrete-population simulation.\\n\\n### Zero correction: `flip7zero_correction`\\n\\n**Paper connection:** Not mentioned explicitly, but this corrects a rare numerical artifact.\\n\\nWhen the replicator dynamics collapse all agents of a given type into profiles with utilities so far below average that rounding produces zero agents for that type, this function rescues the simulation by randomly reinitializing that type's profile distribution. The code notes this is \\\"a 1 in 10,000 chance\\\" event. Without this correction, certain runs would crash or produce invalid results.\\n\\n### Mutation: `muterandoms10_smart` and `repmutation_smart`\\n\\n**Paper connection (\\u00a72.2):** \\\"We also allow for the possibility that an agent's strategy profile is not copied faithfully, or 'mutates.' This is governed by two parameters, m0 and m1. Each agent is selected for mutation with probability m0. If selected, each element in the string expression of the agent's strategy profile is assigned a random value from among the allowable values with probability m1.\\\"\\n\\n**`muterandoms10_smart`** pre-generates 10 timesteps' worth of mutation draws at once (for efficiency):\\n- `mutations10[t][agent]`: a Bernoulli draw with success probability m0, marking whether agent is selected for mutation at timestep t.\\n- `newprofiles10[t][k]`: pre-drawn target profile indices for the k-th mutation event at timestep t.\\n- `muteprofilestrings10[t][k][position]`: per-position Bernoulli draws with success probability m1, indicating which positions in the profile string actually get mutated.\\n\\n**`repmutation_smart`** applies these pre-drawn mutations. For each agent selected for mutation, it constructs a new profile by mixing the old profile with the randomly drawn target profile: each position uses the random profile's value with probability m1 (where `muteprofilestrings10 == 1`), or keeps the old profile's value otherwise. This is the \\\"smart\\\" mutation: instead of replacing the entire profile, only m1-fraction of positions are mutated, giving continuity between parent and child profiles. The result is then converted to a profile index using `repmultipliers` and the relevant profile count arrays are updated. Note that `agentprofiles` is NOT updated during mutation \\u2014 it is rebuilt from scratch each timestep by `genBSreplicator_single_tstep`.\\n\\nThe pre-generation batch of 10 and the refresh every 10 timesteps (`if idxN0%10 == 0`) is a performance optimization that avoids numba's overhead from calling the random number generator on every timestep.\\n\\n### Format conversion: `repconvert` and `execrepconvert`\\n\\nNot mentioned in the paper; these are implementation utilities.\\n\\n`repconvert` and `execrepconvert` translate from the replicator's compact profile-index representation back to the urn-based representation (`sigurns`, `recurns`, `execurns`). This conversion is needed when the simulation wants to call reporting functions that expect urn format (such as `genBS_results` or `time_update`). The exec version additionally fills in `execurns` by reading whether each agent's signal in each dimension is null (0 = not attending) or nonzero (1 = attending).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Part 4: Roth-Erev Reinforcement Learning \\u2014 `genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play` and Supporting Functions\\n\\nThis section covers all functions specific to the RL path.\\n\\n### Main loop: `genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play`\\n\\n**Paper connection (Appendix B):** \\\"nothing about the Generalized Bach or Stravinsky game requires agents to learn according to replicator dynamics. In this Appendix, we give some limited simulation results for the model in which the discrete replicator dynamics is replaced by agents learning according to Roth-Erev reinforcement learning with forgetting.\\\"\\n\\nThis function is the RL counterpart to `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play`. Its overall structure is parallel \\u2014 it runs for up to `runlength` timesteps, checks convergence, records snapshots \\u2014 but the per-timestep update mechanism is entirely different. The key loop comment in the code makes the replacement explicit: \\\"replacing replicator with Roth-Erev.\\\"\\n\\n**Important**: the RL main loop does NOT call any mutation function. The parameter `mutateratef` is passed to the function but unused within `genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play`. Exploration in the RL model comes from two other sources: (1) the stochastic sampling from urns each timestep via `random2picks`, and (2) the floor constraint that keeps every urn option at weight \\u2265 1, ensuring no action is ever permanently eliminated. This replaces explicit mutation.\\n\\n### Initialization: `RothErevExec_initialize`\\n\\n**Paper connection (Appendix B):** \\\"each agent in the population having an urn for each location in the string representation of their strategy profile. Each urn begins a simulation with one ball corresponding to each possible action for that location in the strategy profile string.\\\"\\n\\nUnlike the replicator's `replicatorexec_initialize`, this function does NOT set urns to one-hot vectors. Instead, the notebook sets all urn entries to 1 via `inertia = 1` before calling the simulation. `RothErevExec_initialize` computes only the structural variables `sigperdimf` and `profilecaps` (the size of each urn), without touching the urn contents. The urn entries of 1 at all positions correspond to the paper's \\\"one ball corresponding to each possible action\\\" \\u2014 uniform initial probability over all choices.\\n\\n### Per-timestep profile drawing: `random2picks`\\n\\n**Paper connection (Appendix B):** \\\"In a single timestep, an agent begins by drawing one ball from each of their urns at random with equal probability. These draws then determine the strategy profile that the agent employs for the entire timestep while interacting with every other agent in the population.\\\"\\n\\n`random2picks` performs the stochastic profile draw for all agents simultaneously. For each agent i and each signal dimension d, it draws one signal value from the signal urn proportionally to the urn weights (using the cumulative-sum / threshold method). Similarly, for each possible incoming signal combination (0 through numsignals-1), it draws one action from the corresponding receiver urn. The result is stored in `agentprofilepicks[agent][position]`, a profile-like array holding the specific signal and action choices made by each agent for this timestep.\\n\\nThis implements the paper's \\\"drawing one ball from each urn\\\" \\u2014 the probability of drawing option s from an urn is proportional to the weight of option s in that urn. The pre-generated `picks10` array (10 batches of random draws, regenerated every 10 timesteps) provides the randomness. Using pre-generated randoms is more efficient than calling the RNG inside the tight loop.\\n\\n### RL update with forgetting: `executilcomputeREforget`\\n\\n**Paper connection (Appendix B):** \\\"Reinforcements can be thought of as adding additional balls of the type that was drawn to the urn that it was drawn from \\u2026 at the end of a timestep, forgetting is implemented by multiplying the number of balls of each type by a forgetting factor 0 < \\u03c6 < 1. For any ball type whose quantity falls below 1 in any urn, that quantity is raised to 1.\\\"\\n\\n**Appendix B on assortment:** \\\"To represent assortment, we adjusted agents payoff by multiplying it by H(h,x,i).\\\"\\n\\nThis function is the heart of the RL model. It replaces both `executilcompute` and `genBSreplicator_single_tstep` from the replicator.\\n\\n**Step 1 \\u2014 Forgetting**: Before any reinforcement, every urn entry is multiplied by `forgetf` (\\u03c6 = 0.998). This is applied to both signal urns and receiver urns.\\n\\n**Step 2 \\u2014 Reinforcement**: For each ordered pair (A, B) where A < B (the loop structure `for idx1201mod in range(1, population_size - idx1200)` with modular indexing ensures each unordered pair is processed once, with both agents reinforced in the same call), the function:\\n- Reads A's and B's profiles from `agentprofilepicks` (the draws made at the start of this timestep).\\n- Determines effective signals after null-zeroing.\\n- Determines the actions A and B take.\\n- Computes the assortment multiplier `Ahfmultiplier` for A's signal pairing with B.\\n- If A and B coordinate (same action): `Areinforcement = Ahfmultiplier \\u00d7 (coordination_preference[Atype][action] + signal_cost)`.\\n- If not: `Areinforcement = Ahfmultiplier \\u00d7 (genBSpunish + signal_cost)`. With genBSpunish=0, failed interactions contribute zero reinforcement before the signal cost, meaning signal cost alone is still applied.\\n- Adds `Areinforcement` to A's signal urn entries for each dimension (for the signal A actually broadcast this timestep) and to A's receiver urn entry (for the action A took given B's signal).\\n\\n**Step 3 \\u2014 Floor enforcement**: After all interactions, any urn entry below 1 is raised to 1.\\n\\nA key implementation note not stated in the paper: because this function interacts A with every other agent in the population (not random pairs), the RL model implicitly assumes \\\"a large representative sample\\\" of interactions per timestep, consistent with the paper's general modeling assumption but achieved differently than pairwise sampling. The paper's Appendix B states: \\\"We found that having agents select a single strategy profile that they employ for all interactions on a single timestep made this learning dynamic significantly more computationally tractable.\\\" The `agentprofilepicks` array is what makes this tractable \\u2014 all interactions use the same pre-drawn profile, so we only need to loop over agent pairs and add reinforcements, rather than re-sampling from urns for each individual interaction.\\n\\nThe coordination preference values in the RL notebook are scaled by 1/200 compared to the replicator notebook. This keeps the reinforcement increments small relative to initial urn weights (1 ball each), preventing early interactions from irreversibly dominating urn distributions before agents have explored the space.\\n\\n### RL-specific result reporting: `genBS_resultsRE` and `execrepconvertRE`\\n\\nNot explicitly described in the paper; these are implementation utilities for extracting results from the RL model.\\n\\n**`execrepconvertRE`**: Converts the continuous urn representation to the modal strategy profile used for reporting. For each agent, it reads the argmax of each signal urn (the signal with the highest weight) and maps this to a 0/1 exec value (0 if the modal signal is null, 1 if not). This produces a point estimate of the agent's current \\\"effective strategy\\\" for output purposes only, without affecting the simulation dynamics.\\n\\n**`genBS_resultsRE`**: Analogous to `genBSexec_results` from the replicator, but designed to work directly from the urn-based representation that the RL model maintains. It takes `sigurnsf_4report` and `recurnsf_4report` produced by `execrepconvertRE`. The internal logic of aggregating `socialsig_aggregate`, `action_aggregate`, `simple_stat_001`, and `simple_stat_002` is the same as in the replicator's reporting function.\\n\\n### Remaining RL-only function: `get_sig_countsRE`\\n\\nNot mentioned in the paper; this is an implementation utility.\\n\\n`get_sig_countsRE` tallies the number of agents using each combined signal index in the current timestep by iterating over `agentprofilepicks` rather than `profile_count_untyped` (which the replicator's `get_sig_counts` uses). This is necessary because the RL model does not maintain running counts of how many agents hold each profile \\u2014 instead, profiles are drawn fresh each timestep. The result feeds directly into `find_assort_multipliers`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Part 5: Functions Present in Both Files but Only Used in the RL Full-Play Path in the BZforget File\\n\\nBoth `.py` files contain `genBSreplicator_full_play` (replicator without exec, i.e., without the null-signal attention mechanism), `genBS_full_play` (a lightweight RL-style loop without forgetting), `greetings_full_play` (an even simpler model without generalized payoffs), and `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play` (replicator with exec). These functions represent development history and earlier model versions. In the BZforget notebook, only `genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play_typed` is actually called; the others are present but unused in the active sweep cell. Similarly, the FLIP7 notebook only calls `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play_typed`.\\n\\nThe function `executilcomputeRE` (without forgetting) is present in the BZforget file but not called by the active RL function \\u2014 `executilcomputeREforget` is used instead. The forgetting version simply applies the \\u03c6 multiplier to all urns before reinforcement; the non-forgetting version applies reinforcement directly.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Part 6: Model Description Components Without Direct Code Connections, and Code Components Without Direct Paper Connections\\n\\n### Paper descriptions that connect only implicitly\\n\\n**\\\"Agents do not use signals assortatively to find interaction partners\\\" (\\u00a73.2):** This is the non-assortment baseline. It corresponds to setting `homophily_factor = 0` in the notebooks. With h=0, all entries in `assort_array` equal `base_connection_weights[d]^0 = 1` regardless of d, so `assort_multipliers` becomes a flat matrix of 1/numsignals for all pairs, equivalent to random mixing. The FLIP7 notebook uses `homophily_factor = 1`, the BZforget notebook uses `homophily_factor = 0` in its main sweep.\\n\\n**\\\"T levels of nested embeddings in the group structure require T+1 dimensions of social signals\\\" (\\u00a74.2):** This is a theoretical claim derived from the simulation results, not a code parameter. The number of signaling dimensions is set by `sigdimensions = 2` in both notebooks.\\n\\n**\\\"strategy profiles are transmitted\\\" (\\u00a72.2, \\u00a73.1):** In the replicator, strategy transmission is implemented implicitly through the replicator equation \\u2014 successful strategies become more common without any explicit copying mechanism. There is no function that \\\"copies\\\" a strategy from one agent to another.\\n\\n### Code details not explicitly in the paper\\n\\n**`sigdimensions + numsignals` (not `K + \\u03b8`) profile length:** The paper's \\u00a74.1 states profiles are strings of length K + \\u03b8 where K is the number of signal dimensions and \\u03b8 is the number of possible signal combinations. The code computes \\u03b8 = `np.prod(numsignals_perdim)` (e.g., 2\\u00d72 = 4) and stores profiles as arrays of length `sigdimensions + numsignals` = K + \\u03b8. This exactly matches the paper.\\n\\n**`base_connection_weights` array:** This is `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]` in both notebooks. The index d gives 2^d, which together with `homophily_factor` implements S(h,x,j) = (2^d)^h. This array is technically a generalization allowing non-power-of-2 weights, but in practice the notebooks always use powers of 2 matching the paper's formulation.\\n\\n**Profile count normalization order:** After applying the replicator equation, the code normalizes `profile_count_typed` to maintain constant type sizes and then sums to get `profile_count_untyped`. This order (normalize first, then sum) avoids rounding inconsistencies between the typed and untyped counts.\\n\\n**Convergence criterion details:** The paper says \\\"whether the distribution of agents' strategy profiles was unchanged.\\\" In code, this is `np.array_equal(agentprofilesCOPY, agentprofiles)` \\u2014 an exact match of the integer profile index array for every agent, not just aggregate distributions. This is a very strict criterion (distribution-exact, not just statistically stable), appropriate for a system that is expected to reach a true absorbing state under the replicator dynamics.\\n\\n**Snapshot recording:** Both full-play functions record intermediate `socialsig_aggregate` snapshots at regular intervals during the simulation (`signal_snapshots` parameter, set to 1 in both sweep notebooks). With `signal_snapshots=1`, only one snapshot is taken at the very end (in addition to the final state), and the sweep analyses are all based on final state. The snapshot infrastructure supports more detailed time-series analysis in exploratory cells of the notebooks.\\n\", \"filename\": \"/home/claude/code_paper_mapping.md\"}"

Implementation Details Not Explicitly in Text\n\n1. **`epsilonf` (Numerical Stability):**\n   * **Code:** `csrand = (rngf.random()+epsilonf)*cscumsum[-1]`\n   * **Detail:** Adds `float_info.epsilon` to random draws to ensure sampling from the open interval (0, 1] rather than [0, 1), preventing selection of the lowest-index option when the draw is exactly 0.\n\n2. **`floor` (Discretization):**\n   * **Code:** `stratdex = floor(stratdex)`, `agtype = floor(popt[popdex1])`\n   * **Detail:** Converts mixed-radix profile index computations (which involve floating-point multiplications) into integer array indices.\n\n3. **Cascade rounding (Integer Population Counts):**\n   * **Code:** `intround = np.around(floattotal)`, `incriment = intround-integertotal`\n   * **Detail:** In `genBSreplicator_single_tstep`, floating-point profile counts are converted to integers. The cascade method distributes rounding increments cumulatively across profiles so the total remains exactly `typestotal`. This prevents population drift due to repeated rounding.\n\n4. **`execurnsf` (Attention Tracking — Reporting Only):**\n   * **Code:** Inferred from signal urn argmax at reporting time via `execrepconvert` / `execrepconvertRE`.\n   * **Detail:** Records whether each agent attends to each signaling dimension (1 = attending = non-null modal signal, 0 = ignoring = null modal signal). Used only for output, not during the dynamics.\n\n5. **`profilecaps` (Urn Sizes):**\n   * **Code:** `profilecaps[pcdex] = sigperdim[pcdex]` (for signal positions) or `numactionsf` (for action positions).\n   * **Detail:** Defines how many distinct options exist at each position in the profile string, used in `random2picks` to ensure sampled values are within range.\n\n6. **Cumulative-sum action sampling in `random2picks`:**\n   * **Code:** `csdraw[cscumsum<csrand] = 1; agentprofilepicks[idx8001][idx8000] = np.sum(csdraw)`\n   * **Detail:** Implements weighted random sampling from the urn. The number of entries where `cscumsum < csrand` equals the index of the sampled option. This is equivalent to drawing a ball proportionally to urn weights.\n\n7. **`simple_stat_002` (Strict 75% threshold):**\n   * **Code:** `if socialsig_aggregate[idx9005][cursig] > np.sum(...)*0.75 and action_aggregate[idx9004][cursig][curaction] > np.sum(...)*0.75:`\n   * **Detail:** A stricter version of `simple_stat_001`. Requires that the most common signal accounts for >75% of a type's signals AND that the most common response to that signal accounts for >75% of responses. This is the primary measure used to classify simulation outcomes in the sweep heatmaps.\n\n8. **`genBSreplicatorexec_full_play` vs `genBSreplicator_full_play`:**\n   * **Detail:** The \"exec\" version includes the signal cost and null-signal attention mechanism (`executilcompute` + `execassort_array_create`). The non-exec version (`genBSreplicator_full_play`, present but inactive) uses `utilcompute` without signal cost. Only the exec version is called by the active replicator notebook.\n\n9. **`muterandoms10_smart` (Two-Rate Mutation Logic):**\n   * **Code:** `mutations10 = numbagreater(..., mutateratef[0])`, `muteprofilestrings10 = numbagreater3d(..., mutateratef[1])`\n   * **Detail:** `mutateratef[0]` = m0 (agent-level selection probability); `mutateratef[1]` = m1 (per-profile-position flip probability). An agent must first be selected (m0) before any of their profile positions can mutate (m1). The non-smart `muterandoms10` uses only m0 and replaces the entire profile.\n\n10. **[➕ ADDED] Convergence check interval differences:**\n    * Replicator: checks every 100 timesteps (`if idxN0%100 == 0`) by comparing `agentprofilesCOPY` to `agentprofiles`.\n    * RL: checks every 1000 timesteps (`if idxN0%1000 == 0`) by comparing `agentprofilepicksCOPY` to `agentprofilepicks`. The RL model uses a longer interval because stochastic per-timestep urn sampling means two consecutive stable timesteps will rarely produce identical `agentprofilepicks`, making the exact-equality check less useful at shorter intervals.\n\n11. **[➕ ADDED] Null-signal interaction rule:**\n    * In `executilcompute` and `executilcomputeREforget`, before computing the action each agent takes based on the other's signal, the code zeros out any dimension where *either* agent broadcasts null (0). This implements Section 3.3: \"When an agent does not attend to signals, she interacts with all other agents as if they had also broadcast 0.\" Assortment multipliers, by contrast, are computed from agents' *actual* (pre-zeroing) signal values, since homophily depends on what signals are physically broadcast.\n\n---\n\n### 8. ❌ PRIOR ERROR — Incorrect Section Labels for \"Single\" vs \"Multi\" Embedding\n\n> **[⚠ CORRECTED]** Section 8 of the prior document labeled the replicator notebook as\n> implementing the \"Multi Embedding Structure (Paper Section 4.4).\" **Both notebooks are\n> configured for the single-embedding parameters from Section 4.2 of the main paper** (three\n> types: Lagashites, Girshites, Akkadians; `sigdimensions=2`; coordination preferences from\n> Table 7). Neither notebook is set up for the disjoint double embedding (Section 4.5.1/Figure 12,\n> which requires four types and different signal counts) or the hierarchical double embedding\n> (Section 4.5.2/Figure 13, which requires three dimensions). The replicator notebook provides\n> the replicator-dynamics results for the single embedding; the RL notebook provides the\n> Roth-Erev results for the same single-embedding parameter space, matching Appendix B Table 1.\n\n---\n\n### 9. Reinforcement Learning (Roth-Erev with Forgetting) Implementation\\n\\n**Notebook:** `genBS_v0055k05_BZforget3_assort_f7_RothErevExec_sweep_Merced_topA-Copy34.ipynb`\\n**Script:** `FNs_genBachStravinsky_v0055k05_BZforget3_assort_f7RothErev_rep_execNULLsig.py`\\n**Model Reference:** Supplement Appendix B (\\\"Reinforcement Learning Dynamics\\\")\\n\\nThis notebook implements the **Roth-Erev reinforcement learning** model where agents maintain\\n\\\"urns\\\" (distributions over actions) and update them based on past payoffs.\\n\\n#### Key Code Subfunctions & Model Connections:\\n\\n**A. `genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play_typed` (Wrapper) and `genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play` (Main Loop)**\\n\\n* **Code:** `genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play_typed` is a thin wrapper that converts Python lists\\n  to `numba.typed.List` and back (required for JIT compilation), then calls\\n  `genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play`. Initializes `sigurnsf` (Signal Urns) and `recurnsf`\\n  (Response Urns) with `inertia = 1` (equal weight for all options).\\n* **Model Connection:** Implements the \\\"urns\\\" concept described in the supplement. Each agent has\\n  an urn for each location in their strategy profile string. The initial value of 1 for all urn\\n  entries corresponds to \\\"one ball corresponding to each possible action\\\" (Appendix B).\\n* **Subfunction:** `RothErevExec_initialize`:\\n  * **Code:** Computes structural variables `sigperdimf` (number of signals per dimension) and\\n    `profilecaps` (urn sizes). Does **not** alter urn contents, which are pre-filled with `inertia`\\n    before the call.\\n  * **Model Connection:** Sets up the urn structure described in Appendix B. The urn content\\n    initialization (one ball per option) is actually handled by the notebook setting `inertia = 1`\\n    before the simulation call.\\n* **Subfunction:** `random2picks`:\\n  * **Code:** `random2picks(randoms4pick, sigdimensionsf, sigurnsf, recurnsf, population_sizef, agentprofilepicks, profile_length, profilecaps, numsignalsf)`\\n  * **Model Connection:** Implements the **Action Selection** step described in Appendix B: \\\"In a\\n    single timestep, an agent begins by drawing one ball from each of their urns at random with\\n    equal probability.\\\" For each agent and each signal dimension, it draws a signal value from the\\n    signal urn proportionally to its weights (using the cumulative-sum threshold method). For each\\n    possible incoming signal combination, it draws an action from the corresponding receiver urn.\\n    The result is stored in `agentprofilepicks` \\u2014 the complete strategy employed by each agent for\\n    the **entire** timestep. This corresponds to Appendix B: \\\"These draws then determine the\\n    strategy profile that the agent employs for the entire timestep while interacting with every\\n    other agent in the population.\\\"\\n\\n**[\\u2795 ADDED]** The `picks10` array is a batch of 10 pre-generated random draws (refreshed every\\n10 timesteps) used by `random2picks`. Pre-batching avoids repeated overhead from calling the\\nrandom number generator inside the tight numba loop.\\n\\n* **Subfunction:** `executilcomputeREforget`:\\n  * **Code:** Updates `sigurnsf` and `recurnsf` in three phases:\\n    1. **Forgetting first:** all urn entries multiplied by `forgetf` (\\u03c6 = 0.998).\\n    2. **Reinforcement:** iterates over all agent pairs and adds payoff-weighted reinforcement to the urns used this timestep.\\n    3. **Floor enforcement:** any urn entry below 1 is raised back to 1.\\n  * **Model Connection:** Implements the complete learning rule from Appendix B.\\n    * **Reinforcement:** If agents A and B coordinate (same action), `Areinforcement = Ahfmultiplier \\u00d7 (coordination_preference[Atype][Aaction] + signal_cost)` is added to A's signal urn entries and receiver urn entry for the actions/signals used this timestep. This matches Appendix B: \\\"if an agent receives a non-zero payoff the urns that contributed to their actions are reinforced.\\\"\\n    * **Forgetting:** Multiplying all urn entries by \\u03c6 < 1 matches Appendix B: \\\"forgetting is implemented by multiplying the number of balls of each type by a forgetting factor.\\\"\\n    * **Flooring:** `if sigurnsf[...] < 1: sigurnsf[...] = 1` matches Appendix B: \\\"For any ball type whose quantity falls below 1 in any urn, that quantity is raised to 1; this helps preserve the possibility of that action being chosen in the future.\\\"\\n    * **Assortment:** The payoff is multiplied by `Ahfmultiplier`, computed from `assort_multipliers`, implementing H(h,x,i) from Appendix B's assortment formula: \\\"we adjusted agents payoff by multiplying it by H(h,x,i).\\\"\\n\\n  **[\\u2795 ADDED \\u2014 Important order detail]** Forgetting occurs **before** reinforcement within `executilcomputeREforget`. This means old urn weights are decayed first, and then new payoffs are added on top of the decayed values. This order is not stated explicitly in Appendix B but is consequential for the dynamics.\\n\\n  **[\\u2795 ADDED \\u2014 All-pairs structure]** `executilcomputeREforget` iterates over all ordered pairs using `for idx1201mod in range(1, population_size - idx1200)` with modular indexing. This means each agent effectively interacts with every other agent in the population on each timestep (not random pairs). This is consistent with Appendix B's note: \\\"We found that having agents select a single strategy profile that they employ for all interactions on a single timestep made this learning dynamic significantly more computationally tractable.\\\"\\n\\n  **[\\u2795 ADDED \\u2014 Signal cost in RL]** The signal cost (`sigcostf`) is negative (e.g., -0.000125 in the notebook). It is included in `totalAsigcost = (number of non-null signal dimensions) \\u00d7 sigcostf` and **added** to payoffs on both successes and failures. Since `sigcostf` is negative, this always reduces the reinforcement magnitude for signaling agents. The cost is proportional to the number of active dimensions, matching Section 4.1: \\\"the signal cost c is incurred for each dimension attended to.\\\"\\n\\n  **[\\u2795 ADDED \\u2014 Coordination preferences scaled by 1/200]** In the RL notebook, `coordination_preferences = (np.array([[1.5, 0, .85], [1.25, 1.5+pa, .85], [0, 0, 1]]))/200`. The 1/200 scaling brings payoff values into the range of ~0.005\\u20130.0075, matching Appendix B Table 1 (e.g., Lagashites' Lagash-greeting payoff = 0.0075 = 1.5/200). Keeping reinforcement increments small relative to initial urn weights (1 ball each) prevents early interactions from irreversibly dominating the urn distributions before agents have had time to explore.\\n\\n**B. \\u274c PRIOR ERROR \\u2014 `greetings_check_success` and `genBS_check_success` are not part of the active RL simulation**\\n\\n> **[\\u26a0 CORRECTED]** The prior document described `greetings_check_success` and\\n> `genBS_check_success` as implementing the \\\"Payoff/Coordination Logic\\\" for the RL model.\\n> **Neither function is called by `genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play`**, the active RL simulation\\n> function. These functions belong to older, pair-based RL implementations\\n> (`greetings_single_tstep`, `genBS_single_tstep`) that are present in the RL script but not\\n> invoked by either notebook. All payoff and coordination logic in the active RL model is handled\\n> entirely within `executilcomputeREforget`. The `greetings_check_success` / `genBS_check_success`\\n> functions are legacy code.\\n\\n**C. `execrepconvertRE`**\\n\\n* **Code:** Converts the continuous urn representations (`sigurnsf`, `recurnsf`) into a modal profile representation for reporting. For each agent and each signal dimension, it reads the argmax of the signal urn (the option with the highest weight) and maps this to a 0/1 exec value (0 if modal signal is null, 1 if nonzero).\\n* **Model Connection:** Provides a point estimate of each agent's current \\\"effective strategy\\\" for output purposes. This does not affect the simulation dynamics \\u2014 it is called only at reporting intervals.\\n\\n**[\\u2795 ADDED \\u2014 No mutation in active RL loop]** The `mutateratef` parameter is passed to\\n`genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play` but is **not used** inside that function. The active RL loop\\ncontains no mutation calls. Exploration is provided instead by: (1) stochastic sampling from urns\\nvia `random2picks` each timestep, and (2) the floor constraint (urn minimum = 1) that keeps every\\noption permanently available regardless of its reinforcement history. This replaces the role that\\nmutation plays in the replicator model.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 3. Discrete Replicator Dynamics Implementation\\n\\n**Notebook:** `genBS_v0055k_assort_FLIP7_repEXEC_sm_sweep_Merced_topA-Copy4.ipynb`\\n**Script:** `FNs_genBachStravinsky_v0055k_assort_FLIP7_rep_execNULLsig_SMARTmutation.py`\\n**Model Reference:** Paper Section 2.2 (\\\"Evolutionary Dynamics\\\")\\n\\nThis notebook implements the **Discrete Replicator Dynamics** where strategy profiles (integers)\\nare updated based on their relative utility compared to the population average.\\n\\n#### Key Code Subfunctions & Model Connections:\\n\\n**A. `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play_typed` (Wrapper) and `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play` (Main Loop)**\\n\\n* **Code:** `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play_typed` is the thin numba-typed wrapper. The actual\\n  simulation runs in `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play`. It initializes `execurnsf` and\\n  `profiles_indexed` through `replicatorexec_initialize`.\\n* **Model Connection:** Initializes the population with random strategy profiles. `profiles_indexed` maps integers to the string of signals/actions (length `sigdimensions + numsignals`). This matches the paper: \\\"initially... randomly assigned a behavior strategy to each.\\\"\\n\\n* **Subfunction \\u2014 \\u274c PRIOR ERROR \\u2014 `genBSreplicatorexec_k_step` (not `genBSreplicator_first_tstep`) is the active initializer:**\\n\\n  > **[\\u26a0 CORRECTED]** The prior document listed `genBSreplicator_first_tstep` as the\\n  > initialization function used by the replicator. In `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play`, this call\\n  > is **commented out**. The active initializer is `genBSreplicatorexec_k_step`, which assigns\\n  > each agent a profile index drawn uniformly at random from all `numprofiles` possible profiles.\\n  > `genBSreplicator_first_tstep` is present in the script but inactive.\\n\\n  * **Code:** `genBSreplicatorexec_k_step(numtypesf, rngf, population_sizef, numprofilesf, poptf)` \\u2014 assigns each agent a uniformly random profile index, initializes `profile_count_typed` and `profile_count_untyped`.\\n  * **Model Connection:** Implements the paper's random initialization (Section 2.2).\\n\\n* **Subfunction:** `genBSreplicator_single_tstep`:\\n  * **Code:** `profile_count_typed[idx...][idx...] += profile_count_typed[idx...][idx...] * (profile_utility_bytype[idx...][idx...] - typesaverage[idx...])`\\n  * **Model Connection:** Implements the **Replicator Update Rule**: N_{k,t+1}(x) = N_{k,t}(x) + N_{k,t}(x) \\u00d7 [Uk(x) - Avg(Uk)]. The count of agents using strategy x increases if Uk(x) is above the average utility for their type.\\n  * **Normalization:** `profile_count_typed[idx...] = profile_count_typed[idx...] * (typestotal[idx...] / np.sum(...))`. Ensures population size remains constant per type.\\n  * **[\\u2795 ADDED]** Also performs cascade integer rounding (see Implementation Details section below) and rebuilds the `agentprofiles` array as an ordered list of profile assignments per agent. Negative counts (from the replicator equation when utility is far below average) are clamped to zero before normalization.\\n\\n* **Subfunction \\u2014 \\u274c PRIOR ERROR \\u2014 `executilcompute` (not `utilcompute`) is the active utility function:**\\n\\n  > **[\\u26a0 CORRECTED]** The prior document listed `utilcompute` and `executilcompute` as equivalent\\n  > alternatives. In `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play`, only `executilcompute` is called. The plain\\n  > `utilcompute` function (without the \\\"exec\\\" prefix) lacks signal cost handling and is used in\\n  > older replicator variants (`genBSreplicator_full_play`) that do not include the attention/cost\\n  > mechanism. In the active replicator sweep, it is `executilcompute` that is called.\\n\\n  * **Code:** Calculates `profile_utility_bytype` by iterating over all strategy pairs, incorporating assortment multipliers, signal cost, and payoffs based on `coordination_preferencesf`.\\n  * **Model Connection:** Implements the utility function Uk(x) from Section 2.2 and the assortment-weighted version from Appendix A. For each pair of profiles (A, B): looks up the action A takes based on B's effective signal, applies the assortment multiplier H(h,A,B), and adds `hfmultiplier \\u00d7 M(B) \\u00d7 (coordination_preference[type][action] + signal_cost)` to A's utility. Self-pairings use M(B)-1.\\n\\n**B. \\u274c PRIOR ERROR \\u2014 `muterandoms10_smart` and `repmutation_smart` (not the non-`_smart` versions) are used**\\n\\n> **[\\u26a0 CORRECTED]** The prior document's Section 3B described the replicator as using\\n> `muterandoms10` and `repmutation`. The active replicator function (`genBSreplicatorexec_full_play`)\\n> calls `muterandoms10_smart` and `repmutation_smart`. The non-`_smart` variants are present in\\n> both scripts but are not called by either active notebook.\\n\\n* **`muterandoms10_smart`**:\\n  * **Code:** Generates 10 timesteps of mutation draws at once: `mutations10` (per-agent Bernoulli draws with rate m0), `newprofiles10` (target profile indices), and `muteprofilestrings10` (per-position Bernoulli draws with rate m1).\\n  * **Model Connection:** Implements the two-parameter mutation described in Section 2.2: \\\"Each agent is selected for mutation with probability m0. If selected, each element in the string expression of the agent's strategy profile is assigned a random value from among the allowable values with probability m1.\\\"\\n\\n* **`repmutation_smart`**:\\n  * **Code:** For each agent selected for mutation, constructs a new profile by mixing their old profile with a randomly drawn target profile: each position uses the random profile's value where `muteprofilestrings == 1` (probability m1), or keeps the old value otherwise.\\n  * **Model Connection:** This is the \\\"smart\\\" mutation \\u2014 rather than replacing the entire profile, only m1-fraction of positions change, giving continuity between pre- and post-mutation strategies. The new profile index is then computed and the count arrays updated.\\n  * **[\\u2795 ADDED]** Pre-generating 10 rounds and refreshing every 10 steps (`if idxN0%10 == 0`) avoids the overhead of calling the random number generator inside every numba timestep.\\n\\n**C. `repconvert` and `execrepconvert`**\\n\\n* **Code:** Converts integer `agentprofiles` back into the `sigurnsf`, `recurnsf`, (and for `execrepconvert`) `execurnsf` array format for data logging.\\n* **Model Connection:** Translates the discrete strategy profile (integer index) back to the detailed signal/action urn structure for analysis functions that expect urn format (e.g., `time_update`, `genBS_results`). This conversion is needed only at reporting intervals, not every timestep.\\n\\n**D. `time_update`**\\n\\n* **Code:** Aggregates `recurnsf` into `typed_time` and `signal_time`.\\n* **Model Connection:** Implements the **Time Series Recording**. Records the average frequency of actions given specific signals over time. Used to visualize the evolution of individual simulation runs (not used for any cross-run aggregate statistics reported in the paper).\\n\\n**[\\u2795 ADDED] `flip7zero_correction`**: A numerical safety function. When the replicator dynamics\\ncollapse all agents of a given type into profiles so far below average that rounding produces zero\\nagents for that type, this function randomly reinitializes that type's profile distribution. The\\ncode comments note this is a \\\"1 in 10,000 chance\\\" event. Not mentioned in the paper.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 4. Summary of Model Components in Code\\n\\n> **[\\u26a0 CORRECTED]** The prior document's summary table attributed all functions to a single shared\\n> script. The \\\"Script\\\" column below reflects the correct two-script structure.\\n\\n| Model Component (Paper/Supplement) | Code Subfunction / Variable | Script | Description of Connection |\\n|:---|:---|:---|:---|\\n| **Preference Types** (Ummians, Kishus, Akkadians) | `popt` / `coordination_preferencesf` | Both | Defines population composition and payoff matrices (e.g., Table 5 in paper). |\\n| **Multidimensional Signals** | `sigdimensionsf`, `sigmultipliers`, `sigurnsf` | Both | Allows broadcasting signals across dimensions. `sigurnsf` holds weights for each signal option per dimension. |\\n| **Conditional Actions** | `recurnsf` (both) / `profiles_indexed` (Replicator) | Both | Stores the strategy: \\\"If Signal combo X, do Action Y\\\". The Core Learning Loop (Step-by-Step)\\n\\n> **[\\u26a0 CORRECTED]** The prior document's loop description referenced `genBS_full_play` calling\\n> `greetings_check_success` or `genBS_check_success`. **Neither is called by the active full-play\\n> functions in either notebook.** The correct active call chains are:\\n>\\n> - **Replicator:** `executilcompute` \\u2192 `genBSreplicator_single_tstep`\\n> - **RL:** `random2picks` \\u2192 `get_sig_countsRE` \\u2192 `find_assort_multipliers` \\u2192 `executilcomputeREforget`\\n>\\n> `genBS_full_play` is an older variant present in both scripts but not called by either notebook.\\n\\n| Variable / Function | Replicator Logic | RL Logic (Roth-Erev) | Paper/Supplement Correlation | Implementation Detail |\\n|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|\\n| `agentprofilepicks` | N/A | `random2picks` generates this | **Supplement:** Appendix B | Per-agent profile draws for the current timestep. Implementation Details Not Explicitly in Text\\n\\n1. **`epsilonf` (Numerical Stability):**\\n   * **Code:** `csrand = (rngf.random()+epsilonf)*cscumsum[-1]`\\n   * **Detail:** Adds `float_info.epsilon` to random draws to ensure sampling from the open interval (0, 1] rather than [0, 1), preventing selection of the lowest-index option when the draw is exactly 0.\\n\\n2. **`floor` (Discretization):**\\n   * **Code:** `stratdex = floor(stratdex)`, `agtype = floor(popt[popdex1])`\\n   * **Detail:** Converts mixed-radix profile index computations (which involve floating-point multiplications) into integer array indices.\\n\\n3. **Cascade rounding (Integer Population Counts):**\\n   * **Code:** `intround = np.around(floattotal)`, `incriment = intround-integertotal`\\n   * **Detail:** In `genBSreplicator_single_tstep`, floating-point profile counts are converted to integers. The cascade method distributes rounding increments cumulatively across profiles so the total remains exactly `typestotal`. This prevents population drift due to repeated rounding.\\n\\n4. **`execurnsf` (Attention Tracking \\u2014 Reporting Only):**\\n   * **Code:** Inferred from signal urn argmax at reporting time via `execrepconvert` / `execrepconvertRE`.\\n   * **Detail:** Records whether each agent attends to each signaling dimension (1 = attending = non-null modal signal, 0 = ignoring = null modal signal). Used only for output, not during the dynamics.\\n\\n5. **`profilecaps` (Urn Sizes):**\\n   * **Code:** `profilecaps[pcdex] = sigperdim[pcdex]` (for signal positions) or `numactionsf` (for action positions).\\n   * **Detail:** Defines how many distinct options exist at each position in the profile string, used in `random2picks` to ensure sampled values are within range.\\n\\n6. **Cumulative-sum action sampling in `random2picks`:**\\n   * **Code:** `csdraw[cscumsum<csrand] = 1; agentprofilepicks[idx8001][idx8000] = np.sum(csdraw)`\\n   * **Detail:** Implements weighted random sampling from the urn. The number of entries where `cscumsum < csrand` equals the index of the sampled option. This is equivalent to drawing a ball proportionally to urn weights.\\n\\n7. **`simple_stat_002` (Strict 75% threshold):**\\n   * **Code:** `if socialsig_aggregate[idx9005][cursig] > np.sum(...)*0.75 and action_aggregate[idx9004][cursig][curaction] > np.sum(...)*0.75:`\\n   * **Detail:** A stricter version of `simple_stat_001`. Requires that the most common signal accounts for >75% of a type's signals AND that the most common response to that signal accounts for >75% of responses. This is the primary measure used to classify simulation outcomes in the sweep heatmaps.\\n\\n8. **`genBSreplicatorexec_full_play` vs `genBSreplicator_full_play`:**\\n   * **Detail:** The \\\"exec\\\" version includes the signal cost and null-signal attention mechanism (`executilcompute` + `execassort_array_create`). The non-exec version (`genBSreplicator_full_play`, present but inactive) uses `utilcompute` without signal cost. Only the exec version is called by the active replicator notebook.\\n\\n9. **`muterandoms10_smart` (Two-Rate Mutation Logic):**\\n   * **Code:** `mutations10 = numbagreater(..., mutateratef[0])`, `muteprofilestrings10 = numbagreater3d(..., mutateratef[1])`\\n   * **Detail:** `mutateratef[0]` = m0 (agent-level selection probability); `mutateratef[1]` = m1 (per-profile-position flip probability). An agent must first be selected (m0) before any of their profile positions can mutate (m1). The non-smart `muterandoms10` uses only m0 and replaces the entire profile.\\n\\n10. **[\\u2795 ADDED] Convergence check interval differences:**\\n    * Replicator: checks every 100 timesteps (`if idxN0%100 == 0`) by comparing `agentprofilesCOPY` to `agentprofiles`.\\n    * RL: checks every 1000 timesteps (`if idxN0%1000 == 0`) by comparing `agentprofilepicksCOPY` to `agentprofilepicks`. Mutation\\n\\n- **Paper Description (Sec 2.2, lines 207\\u2013210):** Mutation governed by m\\u2080 (selection probability) and m\\u2081 (element-wise flip probability).\\n- **Code Implementation:**\\n  - `muterandoms10_smart`: Generates random masks based on m\\u2080 and proposes new profile elements based on m\\u2081. Pre-generates 10 rounds of mutations at once for efficiency; refreshed every 10 timesteps.\\n  - `repmutation_smart`: Applies masks to current profiles \\u2014 each profile position uses the randomly drawn value with probability m\\u2081, or retains the old value otherwise. Converts new profile strings to indices and updates `profile_count_typed` and `profile_count_untyped`.\\n\\n  > **[\\u2795 ADDED \\u2014 Unused mutation variants]** `muterandoms10` and `repmutation` (without\\n  > `_smart`) are also present in the script but are **not** called by the active replicator.\\n  > The `_smart` variants are the active ones because they implement the two-parameter (m\\u2080, m\\u2081)\\n  > mutation described in the paper, whereas the non-smart versions use only m\\u2080 and replace\\n  > entire profiles rather than individual elements.\\n\\n**[\\u2795 ADDED \\u2014 Convergence check]** The active replicator loop checks for early termination every\\n100 timesteps by comparing `agentprofilesCOPY` to `agentprofiles`. If they are identical (the\\ndistribution has fully stabilized), the simulation halts before reaching `runlength`. This\\ncorresponds to the paper's footnote: \\\"every 100 timesteps it was checked whether the distribution\\nof agents' strategy profiles was unchanged.\\\"\\n\\n#### 6. Recording & Output\\n\\n- **Code Implementation:**\\n\\n  > **[\\u26a0 CORRECTED \\u2014 \\u274c `genBSreplicatorexec_k_step` is an initialization function, not part of recording/output]**\\n  > The prior document listed \\\"`genBSreplicatorexec_k_step` / `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play`:\\n  > Main simulation loop.\\\" `genBSreplicatorexec_k_step` is the **random profile initialization**\\n  > function called once at the start of the simulation; it has nothing to do with recording or\\n  > output. `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play` is the main simulation loop. These serve completely\\n  > different roles.\\n\\n  - `genBSreplicatorexec_full_play`: Main simulation loop.\\n  - `execrepconvert`: Converts integer profile counts back to one-hot urn structures for reporting.\\n  - `genBSexec_results`: Aggregates behavioral statistics (social signal frequencies, action contingencies, `simple_stat_001`, `simple_stat_002`) from the urn format.\\n  - `time_update`: Records time-series of conditional action probabilities.\\n  - `average_mutual_info` / `getalphasignaling`: Computes Shannon mutual information and identifies \\\"alpha\\\" signals for cross-run aggregation.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### \\ud83d\\udcd7 PART 2: ROTH-EREV REINFORCEMENT LEARNING WITH FORGETTING\\n\\n**Notebook:** `genBS_v0055k05_BZforget3_assort_f7_RothErevExec_sweep_Merced_topA-Copy34.ipynb`\\n**Script:** `FNs_genBachStravinsky_v0055k05_BZforget3_assort_f7RothErev_rep_execNULLsig.py`\\n\\n#### 1. Urn Initialization\\n\\n- **Supplement Description (App B):** Each agent maintains an urn for each dimension/action in their strategy string. Each urn starts with 1 ball per possible action.\\n\\n> **[\\u26a0 CORRECTED \\u2014 \\u274c `RothErevExec_initialize` does not initialize urn entries]**\\n> The prior document states: \\\"`RothErevExec_initialize`: Sets up `sigurnsf` and `recurnsf`\\n> arrays. Initializes all entries to `inertia=1`.\\\" **This is wrong.** `RothErevExec_initialize`\\n> only computes the structural parameters `sigperdimf` and `profilecaps` (the number of signals\\n> per dimension and the size of each urn position). It returns only these two arrays and does\\n> not touch `sigurnsf` or `recurnsf` at all. The urn entries are initialized to `inertia=1`\\n> in the **notebook itself**, before the simulation call, via:\\n> `sigurns = [np.ones([population_size, numsignals_perdim[i]]) * inertia for i in ...]`\\n> `recurns = np.ones([population_size, numsignals, numactions]) * inertia`\\n> This corresponds to Appendix B's \\\"one ball corresponding to each possible action.\\\"\\n\\n#### 2. Timestep Strategy Selection (Computational Tweak)\\n\\n- **Supplement Description (App B):** \\\"We found that having agents select a single strategy profile that they employ for all interactions on a single timestep made this learning dynamic significantly more computationally tractable.\\\"\\n- **Code Implementation:**\\n  - `random2picks`: Draws one discrete action/signal per dimension from each agent's urns for the current timestep. Stores the result in `agentprofilepicks`. This single profile is held fixed for all pairwise interactions during that timestep, exactly matching the supplement's tractability optimization.\\n\\n#### 3. Pairing & Assortment\\n\\n- **Supplement Description (App B):** Payoffs are multiplied by H(h,x,i) based on shared signal dimensions.\\n\\n> **[\\u26a0 CORRECTED \\u2014 \\u274c `connections_init` and `pairings` are not active in the RL model]**\\n> The prior document states the RL notebook \\\"Uses the same assortment infrastructure as the\\n> replicator model (`connections_init`, `pairings`, `assort_array_create`, `find_assort_multipliers`).\\\"\\n> **`connections_init` and `pairings` are NOT called by `genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play`.**\\n> Like the active replicator, the active RL model uses the analytical assortment approach\\n> (`execassort_array_create` and `find_assort_multipliers`), not explicit per-agent pairing.\\n> `connections_init` and `pairings` are legacy functions from earlier pair-based RL variants\\n> that are not invoked by either active notebook.\\n>\\n> Additionally, the prior document mentioned `assort_array_create` (without \\\"exec\\\") as active.\\n> The active RL model calls `execassort_array_create`, which only counts matches in dimensions\\n> where both agents have non-null signals, matching the null-signal attention model.\\n\\n#### 4. Payoff Calculation & Reinforcement\\n\\n- **Supplement Description (App B):** If payoff > 0, reinforce the specific urns that contributed to the action. Add payoff-many balls to the used urns.\\n- **Code Implementation:**\\n  - `executilcomputeREforget`: Core reinforcement loop.\\n    - Iterates through all agent pairs using the fixed timestep profiles from `agentprofilepicks`.\\n    - Computes observed signals (masking unattended dimensions) and retrieves contingent actions.\\n    - Calculates payoff using `coordination_preferencesf`, `sigcostf`, and `assort_multipliers`.\\n    - **Selective Reinforcement:** Adds the calculated payoff (`Areinforcement`/`Breinforcement`) **only** to the specific sender dimension urn entries and receiver urn entries that were actually used in that interaction. Uninvolved urns are untouched. Matches the supplement's urn update rule precisely.\\n\\n#### 5. Forgetting Mechanism\\n\\n- **Supplement Description (App B):** At timestep end, multiply all urn contents by forgetting factor \\u03c6, and floor any urn entry below 1 to 1.\\n- **Code Implementation:**\\n  - `executilcomputeREforget`: At the **very beginning** of the function (before reinforcement), multiplies all `sigurnsf` and `recurnsf` entries by `forgetf` (set to 0.998 in notebook). After reinforcement, enforces `if urn < 1: urn = 1`. This implements the forgetting floor exactly as described.\\n\\n> **[\\u26a0 CORRECTED \\u2014 \\u274c Description of `executilcomputeREforget` incorrectly states it calls `random2picks` internally]**\\n> In Table IV.B, the prior document describes `executilcomputeREforget` as: \\\"2. Draws one\\n> profile via `random2picks`.\\\" **`executilcomputeREforget` does not call `random2picks`.**\\n> The profile draws are performed by `random2picks` in the **main loop** of\\n> `genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play`, before `executilcomputeREforget` is called. The completed\\n> `agentprofilepicks` array is then passed as a parameter into `executilcomputeREforget`. The\\n> two functions are sequential steps in the loop, not nested. The correct order in the main loop\\n> is: `random2picks` \\u2192 `get_sig_countsRE` \\u2192 `find_assort_multipliers` \\u2192 `executilcomputeREforget`.\\n\\n**[\\u2795 ADDED \\u2014 No active mutation in RL]** The `mutateratef` parameter is passed to\\n`genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play` but is **not used** inside that function. There are no mutation\\ncalls in the active RL loop. Exploration is provided instead by: (1) stochastic urn sampling via\\n`random2picks` each timestep, and (2) the floor constraint (minimum urn value = 1) that keeps\\nevery option permanently available regardless of how little it has been reinforced.\\n\\n**[\\u2795 ADDED \\u2014 Convergence check]** The active RL loop checks for early termination every 1,000\\ntimesteps (vs. 100 for the replicator), comparing `agentprofilepicksCOPY` to `agentprofilepicks`.\\nThe longer interval reflects that stochastic urn sampling produces different draws on successive\\ntimesteps even at a stable equilibrium, making exact equality less useful at short intervals.\\n\\n#### 6. Recording & Output\\n\\n- **Code Implementation:**\\n  - `genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play`: Main simulation loop. Replaces the replicator step with `random2picks` \\u2192 `executilcomputeREforget`.\\n  - `execrepconvertRE` / `genBS_resultsRE`: Extracts behavioral statistics from the continuous urn values (using `np.argmax` to determine current behavioral mode) and aggregates them for analysis.\\n  - `time_update`, `average_mutual_info`, `getalphasignaling`: Same analysis functions as the replicator, applied to the RL trajectory.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### \\u2705 COMPLETENESS VERIFICATION\\n\\n> **[\\u26a0 CORRECTED \\u2014 \\u274c Table lists `utilcompute` and `replicator_initialize` as active in the replicator]**\\n> Two entries in this table require correction.\\n\\n| Model Component (Paper/Supplement) | Connected Code Subfunction(s) | Notes |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| Discrete replicator equation | `genBSreplicator_single_tstep` | Exact algebraic translation + cascade rounding |\\n| Utility calculation | `executilcompute` (**not `utilcompute`**, which is inactive) | Handles M(i), coordination preferences, signal costs, assortment |\\n| Mutation (m\\u2080, m\\u2081) | `repmutation_smart`, `muterandoms10_smart` | Bitmask sampling & profile re-indexing; Detailed Explanation: Replicator Dynamics (Notebook 2)\\n\\nThe Replicator Dynamics model simulates the evolution of strategy profiles at the population\\nlevel. Strategy profiles with higher-than-average utility increase in prevalence.\\n\\n#### Core Model Implementation\\n\\n- **The Replicator Equation:** `genBSreplicator_single_tstep` implements the discrete\\n  replicator equation from **Section 2.2**:\\n  N_{k,t+1}(x) = N_{k,t}(x) + N_{k,t}(x) \\u00d7 [U_k(x) - Avg(U_k(i))]\\n  The line `profile_count_typed[k][x] += profile_count_typed[k][x] * (profile_utility_bytype[k][x] - typesaverage[k])` directly executes this update, followed by non-negativity clamping, renormalization to preserve type totals, and cascade integer rounding.\\n\\n- **Utility Calculation (U_k(x)):** The function `executilcompute` (the active utility\\n  function) calculates the expected payoff for strategy profile x for preference type k.\\n  It iterates through all possible profile pairings, calculates the payoff based on\\n  `coordination_preferencesf`, weights by assortment multipliers, and subtracts signal cost\\n  per active dimension.\\n\\n  > **[\\u26a0 CORRECTED \\u2014 \\u274c `utilcompute` listed alongside `executilcompute` as equivalent]**\\n  > The prior document states \\\"The function `utilcompute` (and its extension `executilcompute`)\\n  > calculates the expected payoff.\\\" In the active replicator notebook, only `executilcompute`\\n  > is called. `utilcompute` (without the \\\"exec\\\" prefix) lacks signal cost handling and is used\\n  > only in older, non-exec replicator variants not called by either active notebook.\\n\\n- **Mutation:** Implemented in `repmutation_smart`, using `muterandoms10_smart` to determine\\n  which agents mutate (probability m\\u2080) and which positions in their strategy string change\\n  (probability m\\u2081 per position), per **Section 2.2**. Detailed Explanation: Reinforcement Learning (Notebook 1)\\n\\nThe Reinforcement Learning model (Appendix B) focuses on individual-level urn updates.\\n\\n#### Core Model Implementation\\n\\n- **The Urn Mechanism:** `sigurnsf` (signal urns) and `recurnsf` (receiver/action urns)\\n  represent the per-agent urns described in Appendix B. After\\n  reinforcement, the floor rule raises any urn entry below 1 back to 1.\\n\\n#### Assortment and Interaction\\n\\n> **[\\u26a0 CORRECTED \\u2014 \\u274c CRITICAL: Active RL interaction loop is entirely wrong]**\\n> The prior document describes the RL interaction loop as:\\n> 1. `social_draws`: Agents broadcast signals.\\n> 2. `pairings`: Agents are paired (weighted by assortment).\\n> 3. `receiver_draws`: Agents choose actions based on the partner's signal.\\n> 4. `executilcomputeREforget`: Payoffs are calculated and urns are updated.\\n>\\n> **None of `social_draws`, `pairings`, or `receiver_draws` are called by the active RL\\n> function `genBS_f7_RothErevExec_full_play`.** These are legacy functions from older\\n> pair-sampling RL variants. Exploration is\\nprovided instead by stochastic urn sampling (`random2picks`) and the floor constraint.\\n\\n**[\\u2795 ADDED \\u2014 Convergence check]** The RL loop checks for convergence every **1,000**\\ntimesteps (vs. 100 for the replicator), comparing `agentprofilepicksCOPY` to\\n`agentprofilepicks`. The longer interval reflects that stochastic draws from stable urns\\nproduce different profiles on successive timesteps even at equilibrium.\\n\\n**[\\u2795 ADDED \\u2014 Coordination preferences scaled in RL]** The RL notebook sets\\n`coordination_preferences` divided by 200 (e.g., 1.5/200 = 0.0075), matching Appendix B\\nTable 1.
